commenti.body:
> I am autistic so I take things a bit literal

Literal, as in "that's really someone being harmed" or literal as in "that's just an actor, with makeup and special effects." If the latter, wouldn't that apply to all films? What about a film like Brazil, which has no grounding in reality, but it's an exploitation film either?

The whole point of exploitation films is to be unrealistic. They are called that because they exploit fears and desires. Its like complaining that zombie movies are unrealistic because the dead are coming back to life or that Holocaust films over rely on Nazis. 

The lack of realism is one of the few defining features that make it an exploitation film.

I’m sorry jumbled a bit! 

as in this is all special effects and it definitely can be gross but it doesn’t always have the impact?

I saw Brazil and liked it a lot but got lost near the end 
But it was also intended to be a sci-fi comedy so there’s no real edge lord energy to it? Like sure it’s a criticism of like I think “fascism” and statism, etc but it’s absurdist and that’s kinda clear, tho I can’t always follow films like that and I don’t find them funny in the way it’s intended

> exploitation of Eastern European, African, etc, racism and sexism in films for the sake of shock

But all of those things are real. They all happen in real life. Sure, they're heightened in the genre, but like... I'd wager nothing that's been put on film in a sexploitation/blacksploitation film is really all that far fetched. The trappings of the genre mean they'll be stylized, but that doesn't meant they're not true to reality in some way.
I agree! I probably just am confused by the trappings but also the comments of the directors seem to be contrary to what they produce imo

Well I’m aware of that, it wasn’t a complaint of that, I like all these kinds of films. My inquiry was more in the context in these films specifically something like A Serbian Film, being marked as an allegory or colonialism of Eastern Europe, but then ig either through abstract or bad screenplay that not being articulated enough that the movie is low rated, there’s hella French extremity cinema that are pretty well done, shot, and philosophically sound. my confusion lies in the context in which the films are created, and the intention of the director not correlating and the audience then focusing on the shock value in discuss of horribly prop movies and set designs, with slight continuity issues. 

I may have been jumbled, but my inquiry was on the fact that it’s campy and the interpretation versus the intention are missed In A Serbian Film being a primary example. But the director and some academic writings go over the issue of how the movie was mass distributed through illegal or “controversial” websites and not a more traditional medium.

Exploitation films are base and cartoonish. Occasionally there are exploitation films that transcend these trappings, but those are edge cases. Even still, there are just as many critics who say French Extremity is empty and only posturing to be high minded as there are critics who say that they are "philosophically sound." 

Honestly, I'm still kind of confused as to what youre asking and what youre even saying. I dont really know what youre saying when you say:

"my confusion lies in the context in which the films are created, and the intention of the director not correlating and the audience then focusing on the shock value in discuss of horribly prop movies and set designs, with slight continuity issues"

films are not always meant to be "realistic". Its an art form and some filmmakers use the art form to express ideas that are more extreme or abstract in nature than others. 

There are filmmakers that spoon-feed the audience, and others that do not underestimate the intelligence of their audience and so make it more abstract to express whatever feelings they are trying to get across. 

Watching exploitation films can be tough, and since you're aware that you dislike them, you don't need to watch. Perhaps in the future, you may be curious about them

My take—and I think/hope it gets at your point—is that the whole "oh this boring film about fucking babies is actually a *\~m e t a p h o r\~*" is, imo, nothing more than a marketing ploy built into the movie.

There's a certain amount of people who will watch torture porn for the sake of being edgy/curious/enthralled etc. And then there's a certain amount of people who need some justification for the edginess, so the studios come up with that justification. The "metaphor" angle is just to win those people over. That's it. And to cause more discussion in the media about whether it somehow is really academic somehow. 

"Is the dress blue or gold? What an important discussion everyone is having. And you get to decide for yourself, you empowered consumer! Now just go ahead and buy the tickets :)"

To discuss the artistic merit of Serbian Film is, in my opinion, taking the bait. And, unfortunately, if a movie gets a big enough release it's hard to avoiding taking the bait because the film media landscape tries to make it an unavoidable topic.

Yeah I appreciate the good faith, that was exactly my point especially with modern exploitation films especially as horror and the like become popular due to a lot of trends such. I appreciate the response!
